transcript.text: Hi, the light in my Neff oven has stopped working (model B1ACE4HN0B). Oven works fine otherwise. Can I change the bulb myself and what bulb do I need?

Yes — on the Neff B1ACE4HN0B, the oven lamp is normally a user-replaceable part.

### Bulb specification
Use an:

• 40 W
• 230–240 V
• E14 small Edison screw (SES)
• Oven/appliance bulb rated to at least 300 °C

Do not use an ordinary household candle bulb or a standard LED bulb unless it is specifically rated for use inside ovens at that temperature. Do not exceed 40 W.

### How to replace it
1. Isolate the oven from the mains at the cooker switch/fused spur or consumer unit — don’t rely only on switching the oven off at its controls.
2. Let the oven cool completely.
3. Remove the shelves and place a tea towel in the bottom of the cavity, in case the cover or bulb is dropped.
4. Find the lamp glass cover, normally on the side wall of the oven cavity.
5. Unscrew the glass cover anti-clockwise. It can be tight from heat and grease; use a dry cloth or rubber glove for grip rather than forcing it.
6. Unscrew the old bulb anti-clockwise.
7. Fit the new E14, 40 W, 300 °C-rated oven bulb.
8. Refit the glass cover securely, remove the towel, restore power and test the light.

If a new correct bulb still does not light, or the glass cover is damaged/stuck, it is likely to need an engineer — possible causes include the lamp holder, wiring, or oven electronics.

Thanks. I've isolated it at the cooker switch and let it cool first. The glass cover came off with a rubber glove and the filament on the old bulb looks broken. It's marked E14, 25W, 300C though, not 40W. Which should I buy?

Buy a like-for-like E14, 25 W, 230–240 V, 300 °C oven bulb.

You were right to check the old lamp — matching its marked wattage is the safest choice here. My earlier 40 W suggestion was too generic; some Neff ovens use 40 W lamps, but yours has been fitted with a 25 W oven-rated E14 lamp and it has been working correctly.

Look for wording such as:

> E14 SES oven appliance bulb — 25 W — 230/240 V — 300 °C

Avoid ordinary household bulbs and non-oven-rated LEDs. A 25 W bulb will be fine; just fit it hand-tight, refit the glass cover, then restore power.
